summary: Iteration 26 — Verified the escalation-discoverability fix end-to-end. BACKEND (8/8 pytest passed in 3.82s / test_iteration26.py): (1) owner login/prod login/sales login OK; (2) production posts POST /api/tasks/{id}/updates action=escalate — server creates a follow-up task with source='escalation', assignee_id=owner_id, priority='high', status='todo', parent_task_id=original; owner /notifications unread count increments and the freshest '[Escalation] ...' message is present; (3) production posts action=handoff to sales member — follow-up gets source='handoff' (NOT escalation), assignee_id=sales_id, and sales receives a '[Handoff] ...' notification; (4) GET /api/notifications shape is exactly {notifications:[...], unread:int} with no _id leak; (5) owner GET /api/tasks?mine=true includes the source='escalation' follow-up; (6) regression: /api/inbox and /api/decisions still 200; plain action='note' still works and does not create a follow-up. FRONTEND (owner@sharma.com / demo1234): (a) Inbox top section [data-testid='escalations-section'] renders with heading 'Needs your attention — 9 escalation/handoffs' and 9 rows (1 red 'Escalation' badge for our fresh iter26 test + 8 blue 'Handoff' badges for pre-existing follow-ups — matches E1's note that older follow-ups were tagged 'handoff' before the fix); (b) clicking row [data-testid='escalation-<taskId>'] navigates to /my-work; (c) My Work shows [data-testid='badge-escalation-<taskId>'] = 'Escalation' (red bg) on the fresh iter26 follow-up and [data-testid='badge-handoff-<id>'] = 'Handoff' on the 8 older follow-ups; (d) 'Open in My Work →' cta present per row; (e) refresh() invalidates ['tasks', true] so new escalations show up immediately after action. NON-OWNER (production@sharma.com): Inbox correctly shows the escalations-section ONLY because production has 1 incoming handoff ('Follow-up: TEST_iter24_regression_task' handed off by Rajesh Sharma) — the badge is 'Handoff' (blue) not 'Escalation', confirming production does NOT see their own outgoing escalations (which target the owner). Capture UI is gated to owner. REGRESSION: owner capture surface (voice-record-button, text-directive-input, submit-text-directive) all still present; sign-out flow works. Zero console errors observed on any page.

issues: Row description shows the raw follow-up description including the 'Handed off by X on \'title\'. Context: ...' prefix which duplicates the row title. Consider stripping the 'Handed off by ... on \'<title>\'. Context:' prefix in Inbox.js:274 so the row shows only the note text — cosmetic.

Bell icon (top-right, badge shows 91/28 unread) does not have data-testid='notification-bell' — the visual is correct and count matches /notifications unread, but a testid would help future automation.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1707 — `"source": "escalation" if action == "escalate" else "handoff"` is the correct one-line fix; it discriminates escalation vs handoff at insert time so both /tasks?mine=true and the Inbox filter can render the right badge. Good.

server.py:1678-1683 — for action=='escalate' the code always targets the tenant owner (`{tenant_id, role: 'owner'}`) with notify_level=3 and prefix '[Escalation]'. This is correct behavior — production cannot 'escalate to' anyone but the owner, so their outgoing escalations never appear in their own /tasks?mine=true (assignee is owner). Confirmed by the frontend: production only sees handoff rows in their escalations-section, never their own outgoing escalations.

server.py:1702 — `"assignee_id": to_id if inp.to_id or action == "escalate" else None` — this is correct: escalations always have a specific assignee (the owner), and handoff-by-role leaves assignee_id=None but keeps assignee_role set. The 'mine=true' query needs to match on either (assignee_id==me) OR (assignee_role in my_roles); needs to be verified that role-only handoffs also appear on the intended member's mine list — a test with action='handoff' + to_role= would strengthen coverage, but the current spec only asks for member handoffs which are covered.

Inbox.js:245 — `escalations = tasks with source in (escalation,handoff) and status != done` is inclusive on both source types, so before-fix follow-ups (tagged 'handoff') still surface, which is the correct migration behavior (users don't lose visibility of pre-fix items). Good.

Inbox.js:263 — heading `'Needs your attention — N escalation/handoff' + plural 's'` — reads awkwardly when N=1 ('1 escalation/handoff') but is grammatically defensible; consider `${N === 1 ? 'item needs your attention' : 'items need your attention'}` for polish. Non-blocking.

Inbox.js:267 — clicking a row navigates to '/my-work' as a whole, not to the specific task. A `?highlight=<taskId>` or hash-fragment (`#task-<id>`) with matching scroll/highlight in MyWork.js would make the discoverability even sharper (owner has 9 items and would have to scroll to find the fresh one). Optional enhancement.

Inbox.js:274 — row description renders raw `t.description`, which includes the auto-generated prefix 'Handed off by <name> on \'<title>\'. Context: <note>'. Since the title chip already shows the parent title (via replace(/^Follow-up:\s*/, '')), the description prefix is redundant. Consider extracting just the 'Context: ...' portion or displaying the underlying update.text for a cleaner row.
MyWork.js:384-385 — badge chips are inline in the header; testids badge-escalation-<id> and badge-handoff-<id> are present and correctly discriminate by t.source. Good.
Regression: /notifications shape stayed exactly {notifications, unread} — no accidental rename to 'items'. Matches E1's fix and the earlier RCA comment.
Nice-to-have: expose 'source' in the Tasks list view (Tasks.js) with a filter chip, so owner can pivot 'show me all escalations' from the Tasks page too. Optional.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter26 covers the escalation discoverability fix. Rerun backend: `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=$(grep REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL /app/frontend/.env | cut -d= -f2) pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration26.py -o addopts= -v` — expect 8 pass in ~4s. Key facts for the next agent: (1) POST /api/tasks/{id}/updates payload = {text, action: 'note'|'handoff'|'escalate', to_id?, to_role?}. Escalate ALWAYS targets tenant owner; no to_id/to_role needed for escalate. (2) Handoff requires either to_id (specific member) OR to_role (whole role) — otherwise 400. (3) Follow-up task fields: source='escalation'|'handoff', parent_task_id=original, priority='high' for escalate else inherited, title prefixed 'Follow-up: <parent_title>'. (4) /api/notifications returns {notifications:[{id,message,level,read,entity_type,entity_id,created_at}], unread:int}; message format for escalation = '[Escalation] <author_name> needs you on: <step_or_title[:90]> — "<note[:100]>"'. (5) Frontend testids: escalations-section (wrapper, only rendered when escalations.length > 0), escalation-<taskId> (row button), badge-escalation-<taskId> / badge-handoff-<taskId> (chips on MyWork task cards). Row click always navigates to '/my-work' (no per-task deep link yet). (6) Inbox filter: `source in (escalation,handoff) && status != done` — a follow-up moves out of the section once its status flips to 'done'. (7) POST /api/tasks endpoint appears to not exist for standalone create (my test's initial POST /api/tasks returned 404 fallback); the test correctly falls back to picking an existing prod-assigned task. This is worth noting if you need to seed tasks via API — the flow requires /decisions/{id}/tasks path. (8) The frontend already invalidates ['tasks', true] on refresh so posting an escalation and returning to Inbox shows the new row immediately.
rca of the issue: The originally reported bug was DISCOVERABILITY, not delivery. Backend already delivered escalations (owner had 8 pre-fix follow-up tasks tagged 'handoff' + notifications), but there was no dedicated UI surface highlighting them — they were mixed into My Work with no visual differentiator. Fix (verified): server.py:1707 now tags source='escalation' vs 'handoff' at insert time; Inbox.js:245-281 adds a prominent 'Needs your attention' section pinned above capture, listing every non-done escalation/handoff assigned to the current user with a colored badge + click-through to My Work; MyWork.js:384-385 adds inline badge chips on task cards so users can spot escalation/handoff items in the main list too. All three surfaces work as spec'd. Older follow-ups (before the fix) remain tagged 'handoff' and correctly appear as blue Handoff rows — no data migration needed because the Inbox filter is inclusive of both source types. Only NEW escalations from production going forward will get the red 'Escalation' badge, exactly as E1's fix intended and as visible in the owner Inbox screenshot (1 red row + 8 blue rows).
